input.question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?
input.ground_truth: It’s just tradition at this point. At one point in history encores were real but now every band just does it because it’s the thing every other band does. There are exceptions though, I’ve seen Bad Religion headline numerous times going through a 25-30 song set and just end it with no encore. The Supersuckers announce its time for “the fake encore” about 3 songs from the end...

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends put on a little show for your family. You sing songs and everyone cheers. When you finish, your family claps and claps even louder, asking, "Can you sing one more song?" So, you come back and sing another song just for them. That extra song at the end is called an encore.

But sometimes, grown-up bands plan the encore before the show even starts. They decide, "Let’s save a special song for the end, so everyone is really excited and happy!" This way, the crowd knows there’s something extra coming, and it makes the concert even more fun and surprising. That’s why bands do planned encores—they want to make the end of the show extra special!
